version: Compose Multiplatform 1.12.2 (Jetpack Compose 1.12.1 base); Kotlin 2.4.21; Skiko 0.150.2; kotlinx-coroutines 1.11.0; JVM OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM 25.0.4.1+1-1-24.04.4-Ubuntu; GC G1 Young Generation+G1 Concurrent GC+G1 Old Generation

gc.source: GarbageCollectorMXBean count/time deltas between markers; max = max GcInfo.duration from GC notifications (ms resolution)

ops.ffi: java.lang.foreign (FFM, final API, JDK 25) downcall MethodHandle.invoke; validate/parse/hash linked with Linker.Option.critical(false)

notes: frame_ms = interval between consecutive post-present timestamps: in each withFrameNanos callback (Compose FrameRecomposer.performFrame, which runs at the START of the frame, before measure/layout/draw) the app posts java.awt.EventQueue.invokeLater; Skiko's FrameDispatcher runs update+draw+finishFrame (SOFTWARE_FAST: raster surface -> X11 put image) inside the same EDT event, so the posted runnable runs right after finishFrame returned = the latest public post-render signal. Redraw is continuous (each frame requests the next one and changes content). Pacing (ops.pacing): '60' (default) = Skiko's native limiter kept on (public property skiko.vsync.enabled=true, Skiko default: software redrawer awaits FrameLimiter = 1000/displayRefreshRate) BUT under Xvfb it does not cap (measured ~170 fps on list: the refresh rate Skiko reads natively from X11 is not 60), so the app paces with a public API: at the start of every frame (withFrameNanos callback, EDT, runs before measure/layout/draw of that frame, including frames driven by Compose animations) it parks (LockSupport.parkNanos) until an absolute deadline grid of 16.667 ms, re-anchored after a missed deadline; 'uncapped' = skiko.vsync.enabled=false and no app pacing. Canvas: one Modifier.drawWithCache node (clip Path + graph Path allocated once, graph Path rewind()+10000 lineTo per frame), per-shape pre-built linear-gradient Brush (local coords + translate), drop shadow for 1/10 via the public ShadowContext.createDropShadowPainter(shape, Shadow(radius=8.dp, offset=2,2)) (blurred shadow bitmap cached per size), all clipped by clipPath(rounded rect 1000x600, r=24), shapes bounce inside that rect; tick state read in onDrawBehind => draw-phase invalidation only (no recomposition).
